source_exposure: The MOVECLIM 2013 and S1 sources were already read under v1.278. This is retrospective exploratory follow-up, NOT fresh confirmation.
question: Does the greater number of historically local-loss-affected Azorean native plants sampled on Pico reflect association with low introduced-plant richness within original relatively intact native vegetation, rather than an elevation-only concentration?
unit: author-defined 10x10m plot (4 subplots), not 232 independent subplots; taxon-weighted comparisons treat taxa as the descriptive unit
population: All four source-surveyed Azores islands Pico, Flores, São Miguel, Terceira, all 58 identified plots; no island or species response-selected filtering
native_definition: Exact native/endemic statuses; species-rank canonical binomial; valid source OTV 1..9; exclude mixed establishment statuses
introduced_definition: Exact establishmentMeans introduced, species-rank canonical binomial, valid OTV 1..9; unknown and non-species must NOT be counted as introduced or native
introduced_pressure: Number of distinct strictly introduced taxa observed within author 10x10m plot, across 4 valid subplots, count once per species; sum of max ordinal OTV by species is reported ONLY as sensitivity, not interpreted as percentage cover
groups: Native S1-loss-affected taxon (one of fixed 20) versus all other native plot-detected reference taxa within same island
primary: Pico equal-taxon-weight mean introduced-taxon pressure across focal occupied plots minus same metric averaged across Pico other-native species; negative sign favors relative low-introduced exposure; report difference regardless of sign
secondary: Relative elevation-conditional contrast: split Pico's 24 plots into low/high 12 by frozen plot-elevation ordering with deterministic source locationID tie break, center introduced richness within half, then average occupied-plot residual within each taxon and compare focal-reference

All 4 islands report original source plot counts, introduced richness range, strict focal/reference taxon counts, focal-present plots, and group exposure means, suppress group comparison when fewer than 2 focal taxa
Within Pico report introduced-positive plot count, native/focal/reference plot-incidences, and plot-level focal-positive versus focal-negative pressure where groups exist
Use OTV ordinal intensity only for a sensitivity proxy, not for percent alien cover
eligibility_guards: Recompute original v1.278 58/232/2539 and 20/24 and all four island 5/1/1/1 focal, 26/7/3/9 focal-positive plot taxon totals and 746 eligible native plot taxon positives; STOP if mismatch
output: Aggregate counts and descriptive differences only. No species names, source site IDs, coordinates or plot-by-species table in committed outputs or logs; no uncorrected causal p-values
biological_limitations: Plots purposefully sampled relatively intact native vegetation; no comparison with disturbed/island-wide habitat
Introduced species co-occurrence and cover ranks are not exogenous invasion treatment or direct competitive impact
Historical extinction status does not date demographic viability or establish that Pico supplied immigrants
Single census cannot identify persistence, survival, rescue, or movement
Small fixed focal group five taxa on Pico; associations could reflect taxon traits and historic range breadth rather than invasion
Recorded non-native incidence depends on plot sampling/detection and altitude
